title: The Rocky Horror Show on Broadway #rockyhorror #rockyhorrorbroadway #...
transcript: I forgot how much of a mess Rocky Horror is, but this revival certainly reminded me. It boasts a reliable cast and creative team and you mostly get what you would expect from them — no more, no less. I was very impressed by Luke Evans who has a deep, commanding voice but a surprisingly versatile vocal range when singing. Andrew Durand and Stephanie Hsu are marvelous as Brad and Janet, and Amber Gray is a perfectly spiky Riff Raff. I unfortunately found Rachel Dratch as the narrator to be both underused and the harborer of rather tedious material that consistently interrupted the flow of the story. In general, I thought it was a choppy experience, not something that easily whisked me away. Perhaps this is why the emotional apex in Act 2 wasn't very cathartic while Act 1 was a party — I kind of wish they omitted the intermission. Another factor of Rocky Horror that can be difficult to navigate is the audience involvement. In the case of my performance, things were more clunky from the actors anticipating the callbacks than the callbacks themselves. I was actually surprised by how well-behaved we were, though I was at a Saturday matinee — I'm sure Friday and Saturday nights are much rowdier. For a musical that relies so heavily on the energy it conjures up in a room, I'm not convinced this one is built for Broadway — but of all Broadway venues, Studio 54 seems fitting given its history. Although the theatre has been decked out in sci-fi garb and houses an all-star cast, this still feels like a community theatre show, just with a Broadway budget. And for how well-produced it is, it feels safe, void of any real intrigue or point of view that would move the material forward in a particular way. Despite all of these observations that crystallized for me after the experience itself, the production was a great time, no doubt about it. Whether you love Rocky Horror or you're a newcomer to it, this revival shouldn't disappoint. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
